one_liner: C++17 reflection via Clang code generation; serializes structs to JSON, YAML and binary, charted 3.3x faster JSON writes than nlohmann/json.
what_it_does: You mark classes with [[er::reflect]] (plus er::alias and er::ignore on fields), run the er_gen generator over the headers listed in config.yaml, and link the generated reflection.cpp with the `reflection` library. You then call er::serialization::json::to_string(&obj) or json::from_string<T>(str) (also simd_json::from_string, yaml and a variable-length-quantity binary format), which return Expected<T>, plus enum-to-string, method invocation and debug printing. It reads and writes typed structs only (no DOM), so it is not a drop-in for nlohmann/json, RapidJSON or yaml-cpp.
how_it_is_fast: The generator emits per-type field tables, so serialization walks a type-erased TypeInfo tree and appends straight into a std::string through a virtual IWriter, and deserialization writes values directly into struct fields with no intermediate DOM. The native JSON parser is a RE-flex generated DFA lexer (adapted from Robert van Engelen's RE-flex JSON example) feeding a recursive-descent parser; the optional simd_json path parses with simdjson's DOM parser and copies the tape into fields. Part of the charted gap is skipped work, not technique: the JSON writer never escapes strings, the native lexer never decodes escapes, numbers go through unchecked strtoll/strtoull/strtod, and the YAML writer emits every string as an unquoted plain scalar.
when_to_use: Learning or prototyping attribute-driven reflection with Clang code generation on C++17: enum-to-string, field iteration, method calls and debug printing without hand-written glue.
Round-tripping your own structs where the same library writes and reads the data and strings are plain text (no quotes, backslashes, control characters or \u escapes).
Small typed documents (the benchmark used one 2.9 KB profile) parsed through the simd_json path, which is the only JSON reader here that decodes escapes properly.
Compact storage of your own structs: the repo chart puts the VLQ binary encoding at 61% of the JSON byte size.
when_not_to_use: Production use: the README calls the project mostly a proof of concept and recommends glaze instead, and the repository has been archived read-only since 2026-08-20.

Any JSON or YAML exchanged with other software: strings containing quotes, backslashes or newlines produce invalid JSON on write, escaped input is stored undecoded by the native parser, and YAML strings such as true, 123 or 'a: b' are written unquoted and change type or structure on reload.

Untrusted or loosely shaped input: parse_bool treats any token other than false as true, number conversions are unchecked, and an unknown key makes the native parser's get_field(...).unwrap() throw std::runtime_error instead of skipping the field.

Floating-point data: doubles are written with std::fixed and setprecision(9), so magnitudes below about 5e-10 print as 0.000000000 and round trips keep only 9 decimal places; the repo's own threshold tests compare floats with a 0.1 tolerance.

Teams that cannot build a patched LLVM from source (about 45 minutes on a GitHub runner per readme/installation.md) whenever reflected types change; generated files can be committed, but regenerating needs that toolchain.

integration.form: static lib (`reflection`) plus a code generator binary (er_gen) that emits one .h/.cpp per reflected type
integration.dependencies: RE-flex (git submodule, linked statically) and simdjson (default, disable with -DUSE_SIMD_JSON=OFF); er_gen needs a patched LLVM/Clang built from source, inja and tclap; benchmarks add Google Benchmark, RapidJSON and yaml-cpp; all fetched through a vcpkg submodule
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.19+; CI builds the generator and tests in Release on Ubuntu 22.04
integration.platforms: README claims Linux, macOS and Windows on x86 and ARM; CI covers only Ubuntu 22.04 x86

gotchas: Correctness bug behind the serialization numbers: json.cpp writes std::string contents between quotes with no escaping, and the native lexer rule [^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)* assigns the raw string body, so \n, \" and \uXXXX stay undecoded. The benchmark document (boba_fett.json) has no backslashes, so its output happens to be valid, but the timed er writer skips the per-byte escape scan that nlohmann's dump_escaped (with strict UTF-8 checking) and RapidJSON's WriteString escape table perform; the 3.3x serialization gap is not like-for-like. The round-trip tests use CharSet::WoSymbols strings and never exercise escapes.

The yaml-cpp ratios (about 98x write, 15x read) compare an emitter that writes strings as unquoted plain scalars against yaml-cpp's full YAML::Node emitter and loader; treat them as an upper bound on unequal work, not a like-for-like speedup.
The JSON scalar rule needs a value followed immediately by ',', '}', ']' or '\n' (lookahead (?=[,}\]\n])), so input like [1 ] or CRLF line endings after a number or boolean does not match it.

Every array element is parsed into a heap-allocated Box and then copied into the container (no move support, issue #9 open), and the simd_json path constructs a new simdjson dom::parser and a padded_string copy on every call.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: for JSON from reflected structs, glaze (the author's own recommendation) or simdjson's experimental_json_builder (C++26 reflection, no external generator) are the safer picks, and for binary, struct_pack, bitsery or YAS. Choose Easy Reflection only to study a Clang-attribute reflection design that also covers runtime enum strings, method invocation and YAML on C++17.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Google Benchmark (benchmarks/serialization.cpp) on one 2.9 KB document, chart labelled only Core i5, no compiler, flags or build type in the repo: typed-struct JSON write 2.8 us vs nlohmann/json DOM dump 9.3 us and read 17.4 vs 20.8 us (5.7 us via simdjson), YAML write 3.4 vs 331.8 us and read 18.1 vs 274.5 us against yaml-cpp, with RapidJSON at 3.4 us write and 7.4 us read; outputs are not checked for equivalence and the writers skip escaping and quoting.
status_note: Archived read-only since 2026-08-20 (last code change 2025-02-04), Apache-2.0 and copyable, but a self-described proof of concept with string-escaping and YAML-quoting bugs; use it as a design reference, not a dependency.
